title: Keep a shipment's dispatch time from moving

blocks.text: The warehouse service records each parcel's dispatch moment from an old carrier API that still speaks `java.util.Date`, and the type has to stay. Two bugs came in. The scanning station creates shipments in a loop and reuses one `Date` object for every scan; at the end of a shift every parcel of the batch shows the dispatch time of the last one. And since the daily report started adding two hours to the times it prints, late-dispatch alerts fire for parcels that left on time.

Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/Shipment.java`: `keep(...)`, which the constructor calls with the caller's `Date`, and `handOut(...)`, which `dispatchedAt()` calls. When you are done, no caller can change a shipment's dispatch moment through a `Date` it passed in or got back. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a shipment reports the dispatch moment it was created with and compares it with a cut-off
a caller that changes the Date it passed in, to reuse it for another parcel, does not change this shipment
a caller that changes the Date it got back does not change the shipment

origin.section: A Date Is a Mutable Moment, So Anyone Holding It Can Move It

concepts: A java.util.Date can be changed with setTime by anyone holding it, so a class that keeps one copies it on the way in and on the way out.
